title: Unramified morphisms descend along affine-transition limits
statement: Let $I$ be a nonempty directed set and $(S_i)_{i\in I}$ an inverse system of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] with affine transition morphisms [pqf-def-affine-morphism] and limit $S$ [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. Fix $i_0\in I$, quasi-compact quasi-separated $S_{i_0}$-schemes $U_0,V_0$, and an $S_{i_0}$-morphism $g_0:U_0\to V_0$. For $i\geq i_0$ put $U_i=U_0\times_{S_{i_0}}S_i$, $V_i=V_0\times_{S_{i_0}}S_i$, and let $g_i:U_i\to V_i$ be the induced morphism; define $g:U\to V$ similarly over $S$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Assume $g_0$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and $g$ is unramified [def-weil-unramified-morphism]. Then there exists $i\geq i_0$ such that $g_i$ is unramified. No flatness, finite presentation or Noetherian assumption on $g_0$ is required.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-lft-finite-relative-affine-atlas] to $g_0$ over $S_{i_0}$. Obtain the finite charts $W_{j,0},Y_{j,0},X_{jk,0}$ and their rings $R^{(j)}_0,B_{j,0},C_{jk,0}$, with each $\varphi_{jk,0}:B_{j,0}\to C_{jk,0}$ of finite type. These have exactly the quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness hypotheses in the statement.

source.place: Tag 0C4W (lemma-descend-unramified), proof, first paragraph: the finite affine chart reduction in Situation (situation-descent-property).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-affine-limit-chart-diagrams] to these charts and the given inverse system. It gives $R^{(j)}=\varinjlim_{i\geq i_0}R^{(j)}_i$ and affine coverings $X_{jk,i}\to Y_{j,i}$, and $X_{jk}\to Y_j$ at the limit, whose ring maps are $R^{(j)}_i\otimes\varphi_{jk,0}$ and $R^{(j)}\otimes\varphi_{jk,0}$. It also supplies the cartesian chart squares for every $i_0\leq i'\leq i$, including the compatible tensor-product isomorphism needed for stage changes.

source.place: Tag 0C4W (lemma-descend-unramified), proof, first paragraph: the finite affine chart reduction in Situation (situation-descent-property).

proof.text: For each $(j,k)$, restrict the unramified $g$ to $X_{jk}\to Y_j$ using [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-base-change-open] (2). By [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-ring-map-iff-unramified-affine] its ring map is unramified. Apply [lem-trf-colimit-unramified-algebra] to $A_i=R^{(j)}_i$ on the nonempty directed tail $i\geq i_0$ and the finite type $\varphi_{jk,0}$ from step 1. It gives $i_{jk}\geq i_0$ where the chart ring map is unramified, and the same affine criterion gives unramifiedness of $X_{jk,i_{jk}}\to Y_{j,i_{jk}}$. Choose a common upper bound $i\geq i_0,i_{jk}$ by repeated directedness for the finitely many pairs; if there are none take $i=i_0$. By the cartesian squares of step 2, each $X_{jk,i}\to Y_{j,i}$ is a base change of its unramified chart at $i_{jk}$, so [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-base-change-open] (1) makes it unramified. The affine criterion says each of these ring maps is finite type with vanishing differentials. The charts cover $U_i$ and map into the affine opens $Y_{j,i}$ of $V_i$, so the affine-cover characterization in [def-weil-unramified-morphism] gives unramifiedness of $g_i$.

lean.statement: theorem unramified_limit_descent {I : Type u} [Preorder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)] [Nonempty I] (D : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ Scheme.{u}) [∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, CompactSpace (D.obj i)] [∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, QuasiSeparatedSpace (D.obj i)] [∀ {i j : Iᵒᵖ} (f : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (D.map f)] (c : Cone D) (hc : IsLimit c) (i₀ : I) (U₀ V₀ : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace U₀] [QuasiSeparatedSpace U₀] [CompactSpace V₀] [QuasiSeparatedSpace V₀] (u₀ : U₀ ⟶ D.obj (op i₀)) (v₀ : V₀ ⟶ D.obj (op i₀)) (g₀ : U₀ ⟶ V₀) (hg₀ : g₀ ≫ v₀ = u₀) [LocallyOfFiniteType g₀] (hg : IsUnramified (baseChangeHom u₀ v₀ g₀ (c.π.app (op i₀)) hg₀)) : ∃ (i : I) (h : i₀ ≤ i), IsUnramified (baseChangeHom u₀ v₀ g₀ (D.map (homOfLE h).op) hg₀)
